elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: As redlined, 13.5 reads "...("DEVELOPMENTS"), shall be owned by Corio." The carve-out handing ownership to Commerce One where it supports the Developments on an ongoing basis is deleted, so Corio (Customer) owns the Developments outright.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained: "To the extent that Commerce One would otherwise have a claim of ownership in such Developments, Commerce One hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio."

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 2.8 retained ("Commerce One hereby retains all of its right, title, and interest in and to the Software...") and 13.5 remains "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Commerce One hereby grants Corio a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use such materials or technology as part of the Developments" for Commerce One materials embedded in the Developments.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly states the licence is "irrevocable".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly states the licence is "royalty-free".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Inserted data sentence: "As between the parties, Corio retains all right, title and interest in and to all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Corio or its Customers" — covers every category of Customer data, not selected types.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same sentence: "Commerce One shall not use such data other than to process it solely to provide the services under this Agreement" — no resale, independent exploitation or broader "purposes contemplated" carve-out remains.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Proviso added to the closing sentence of 13.5: "...shall be negotiated by the parties prior to the start of any such development work, provided that the parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property."

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 2.8 (Software ownership) and the "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio" opener are retained unchanged.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Corio owns the Developments outright, and the only licence needed (embedded Commerce One materials) is expressly "perpetual".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Embedded-IP licence is expressly "irrevocable"; underlying Developments are Corio-owned.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The inserted licence reads "perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free" with no territorial qualifier; "worldwide" is absent. (Immaterial at the preferred level, where Corio owns the Developments.)

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is limited to "use such materials or technology as part of the Developments"; no modification right is granted over the embedded Commerce One materials.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right appears in the inserted embedded-IP licence (use only, as part of the Developments).

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall not use such data other than to process it solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all nine preferred elements are met in operative language (ownership flip deleted, existing Commerce One assignment retained, pre-existing IP carve-out retained, embedded-IP licence inserted as perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free, no-joint-ownership proviso added, and a Customer Data ownership/use-limitation sentence added).

The walk-away trigger is cured: the only assignment of IP now running to the Vendor — the "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" flip — has been removed, and no assignment of Corio data or IP to Commerce One remains.
Fallback is not independently complete (no "worldwide", modification or sublicensing rights in the embedded-materials licence), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimality holds: the edit removes only the ownership-flip words, retains all favourable existing language (2.8, the Commerce One assignment, the Employee NDA/Invention warranties, the non-disclosure covenant), and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or other extra-checklist requirement. The data sentence is a concise insertion for a genuinely missing clause and covers all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Corio and its Customers rather than selected types.

Intent is preserved: the retained sentence about negotiating ownership of Software enhancements still functions (the new proviso only bars joint ownership as an outcome), the assignment sentence still reads coherently after the deletion, and no cross-reference or defined term is orphaned.

Drafting nits to tidy (not defects in element coverage): the new data sentence is rendered without a section number — give it a number (e.g. 13.6) and anchor it in Section 13 rather than after the successors fragment; and consider using the defined "Corio Services" instead of lower-case "services under this Agreement" so the processing limitation tracks a defined scope.

Optional hardening for the fallback belt-and-braces: add "worldwide" and "and to modify and sublicense such materials as part of the Developments" to the embedded-IP licence if Commerce One resists the ownership position and the negotiation falls back to a licence construct.
